long_biography.plain_text:
The U-Haul stake that made Mark V. Shoen wealthy began with shares distributed by his father, company founder Leonard Shoen. Mark and his brother Joe joined the family faction that accumulated control of the parent company, and Mark later served on its board and led Phoenix operations. He left those corporate posts while retaining a substantial economic and voting interest.

Shoen also developed a separate property platform around self-storage. Companies controlled through Blackwater Investments acquired and developed storage sites, while U-Haul managed many of them, leased facilities and operated dealerships at selected properties. That arrangement kept his private real-estate holdings connected to the family company without making him U-Haul's day-to-day operator. He remains part of the shareholder group whose voting power controls U-Haul Holding Company.
